q-183360.problem: If $A$ is false and $B$ is true, then $A⇔¬B$ is{{field-1}}.
q-183360.worked_solution:
According to the definition of the biconditional, 

- $P⇔Q$ is true if $P⇒Q$ **and** $Q⇒P.$ Otherwise, it is false.

- In other words, $P⇔Q$ is true if $P$ and $Q$ have the same truth values. Otherwise, it is false.

So, when $A=\text{F}$ and $B=\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(A⇔¬B) & =(\text{F}⇔¬\text{T}) \\  & =(\text{F}⇔\text{F}) \\  & =\text{T}.\end{aligned}
$$

The complete truth table is shown below:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬B\,$ | $\,A⇔¬B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
|  |  |  |  |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |

q-83224.name: Question 11
q-83224.problem:
$$
P⇔(P∧Q)≡[P⇒(P∧Q)]∧\bbox[3pt,white,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAAAAAA}}
$$

What expression should be inserted into the blank space above to give logically equivalent statements?
q-83224.worked_solution:
According to the definition of the biconditional, 

- $A⇔B$ is true if $A⇒B$ **and** $B⇒A.$ Otherwise, it is false.

- In other words, $A⇔B$ is true if $A$ and $B$ have the same truth values. Otherwise, it is false.

So, in this case, we have

$$
P⇔(P∧Q)≡[P⇒(P∧Q)]∧[\,(P∧Q)⇒P].
$$

Therefore, the missing part is $(P∧Q)⇒P.$

q-107221.problem:
$$
¬(Y∧X)⇔Y≡[¬(Y∧X)⇒Y]∧\bbox[3pt,white,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAAAAAA}}
$$

What expression should be inserted into the blank space above to give logically equivalent statements?
q-107221.worked_solution:
According to the definition of the biconditional, 

- $A⇔B$ is true if $A⇒B$ **and** $B⇒A.$ Otherwise, it is false.

- In other words, $A⇔B$ is true if $A$ and $B$ have the same truth values. Otherwise, it is false.

So, in this case, we have

$$
¬(Y∧X)⇔Y≡[¬(Y∧X)⇒Y]∧[\,Y⇒¬(Y∧X)].
$$

Therefore, the missing part is $Y⇒¬(Y∧X).$
